headline: High risk of shared-filesystem prompt injection and data leakage; Langflow’s server-side flows amplify Claude Code’s terminal/file trust boundary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code reads repo/user files and uses MCP; Langflow can ingest uploaded files and chain tools in flows. That creates a plausible path where Langflow-produced content is treated as trusted input by Claude Code, especially through shared files or copied artifacts. The interaction is documented only at profile level, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Langflow writes attacker-controlled text into a file that Claude Code later reads as instructions
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or uploaded artifact
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Disable automatic ingestion of Langflow-generated files by Claude Code
Add a human review step before Claude Code reads Langflow outputs
Prefix Langflow outputs with machine-readable data only
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code handles git credentials and arbitrary repo files, while Langflow stores per-flow credentials and can read uploaded files on the server. Both have broad network egress, so sensitive code or secrets can flow from one agent into the other’s outputs or external APIs. Because shared workspace and server-side stores are plausible by default, the blast radius includes exfiltration.
conditions: IF both agents access the same repository or uploaded file set
IF Langflow flows send file contents to configured model providers or HTTP services
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspaces
Rotate any credentials exposed to either agent
Restrict Langflow flows from reading sensitive files
Use separate service accounts and API keys
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and execute shell commands; Claude Code also modifies git state, while Langflow can run unsandboxed Python server-side. In a shared repo or server store, concurrent writes can corrupt files or git history. The profiles show overlapping mutable surfaces without locking, so the conflict is dangerous by default in shared deployments.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same working tree or server-side store
IF Claude Code and Langflow run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes with a simple manual lock file
Avoid concurrent git operations
Run Langflow in a separate container or VM
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared mutable state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow’s graph-based flows can chain multiple agents, and Claude Code can act on files and shell commands. If Claude Code-generated text is fed into Langflow without verification, Langflow may propagate or operationalize errors into downstream actions. The pair therefore supports an A-to-B authority chain with real action-taking impact, making cascading mistakes likely and costly.
conditions: IF Claude Code output is used as a Langflow node input without validation
IF a Langflow flow triggers API calls or other side effects based on that input
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require structured outputs from Claude Code
Disable auto-execution of Langflow flows from agent text
Review downstream actions before enabling them
requires-engineering: add schema checks and confidence gates

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code explicitly handles git credentials and repo files, while Langflow stores per-flow credentials and processes uploaded files on the server. If regulated data is placed into both systems, retention and residency controls may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is appropriate for policy mismatch risk rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Langflow flows and also present in Claude Code’s repo or environment
IF the deployment’s retention or residency policies differ between the two systems
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools
Align retention settings before use
Document which data class each agent may store
Purge flow stores and local repos after runs
requires-engineering: implement policy-based retention enforcement
